segments.name: Access
products: technical support, training and reconditioning services
segments.description: Designs and manufactures access and material handling equipment, including aerial work platforms and telehandlers, for equipment rental companies, construction contractors and home improvement centers.
segments.evidence: The Access segment designs and manufactures access and material handling equipment for use in a wide range of construction, industrial, agricultural, vegetation management and maintenance applications to safely position workers and materials at height under industry-leading brands, JLG and SkyTrak.

segments.name: Vocational
products: Oshkosh S-Series front-discharge concrete mixer vehicles
segments.description: Designs and manufactures fire apparatus, airport equipment, refuse collection vehicles, concrete mixers and command vehicles for municipal and commercial customers in North America.
segments.evidence: The Vocational segment includes the Pierce, Maxi-Metal, Oshkosh AeroTech, Oshkosh Airport Products, McNeilus, IMT, Oshkosh S-Series and Frontline Communications businesses.

segments.name: Transport
segments.description: Designs, manufactures and sustains specialty vehicles and mobility systems for the U.S. Department of Defense, approved foreign customers and the U.S. Postal Service.
segments.evidence: Under the Oshkosh Defense brand, the Transport segment designs, manufactures and sustains best-in-class specialty vehicles and mobility systems for the U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) and approved foreign customers.

revenueModel.text: The company earns revenue from sales of purpose-built vehicles and equipment to equipment rental companies, contractors, municipalities, commercial customers and the U.S. government, largely under multi-year contracts, plus parts, service and financing arrangements.
revenueModel.evidence: The Company generated approximately 20% of its net sales in both 2025 and 2024, and 19% in 2023, from sales to the United States (U.S.) government, a substantial majority of which were under multi-year contracts and programs in the defense vehicle market.

changes.text: In 2024, the Company acquired AUSA, a Spanish manufacturer of wheeled dumpers, rough terrain forklifts and telehandlers.
changes.evidence: In September 2024, the Company acquired AUSA, a privately held Spanish manufacturer of wheeled dumpers, rough terrain forklifts and telehandlers, for $114.5 million.

changes.text: In 2023, the Transport segment sold its snow removal apparatus business and the Vocational segment sold its rear-discharge concrete mixer business.
changes.evidence: In July 2023, the Transport segment sold its snow removal apparatus business for $17.1 million.

changes.text: In 2023, the Company acquired AeroTech and Hinowa, adding airport ground support equipment and compact crawler booms businesses.
changes.evidence: In August 2023, the Company acquired AeroTech from JBT Corporation for $804.6 million.
